summary: The core is one flat netlist-style module (core.v) built from instances of 74161 counters, 74139/74138 decoders and the two Sega PALs written out as gate equations, with registers named by board location (2J, 8H, 3L, 2L, 4L, 3B, 3C, 4A, 4K). Video is a scan-time pipeline: H/V counter bits generate tile/colour latch strobes, ROM data goes into shift registers, and a gate-level priority select picks each pixel. It has CPU wait-state contention for VRAM, which MAME leaves out. Nothing follows MAME's tilemap callbacks, screen_update draw order or *_w handler split.

findings.mame_ref: bankp.cpp: screen raw params (not modeled as counters)
findings.note: The H and V counters are cascaded x74161 instances (u1G/u1H, u1D/u1E) with carry-out wired to load and odd preload values (0110, 0111, 1100), the way the board sets its line and frame length. MAME only gives screen dimensions.
Load, character-latch and colour-latch strobes for both layers come from AND/NOT terms on H counter and scroll-counter bits, i.e. PAL outputs, not a sequencer.

Registered sum-of-products terms (rf14/rf15/rf16, o13) generate VRAM write enables and a Z80 WAIT for CPU accesses during active display. MAME has no such bus contention; its VRAM writes are always immediate.

Memory and I/O chip selects come from cascaded x74139 (u7A, u7B, gated by MREQ/RFSH) and x74138 (u6D/u6E) outputs, not from an address-map case. The resulting map matches MAME's, as any correct core must.

findings.signal: VRAM layout as physical RAM chips
findings.note: Each layer uses one 2KB RAM whose address is muxed between CPU and video (3E-3J muxes), and an H bit picks code or attribute bytes within each tile fetch. MAME splits these into separate videoram/colorram shares with dirty-marking handlers.

findings.signal: Scroll as a loadable counter pair
findings.note: Horizontal scroll comes from latch u2J preloading x74161 counters u2H/u2I at line start, and the counter output (sh) drives the FG RAM address. MAME just calls set_scrollx with 240 - m_scroll_x.

Code and attribute bytes are caught in latches r3l/r2l/r4l/r3b/r3c on PAL strobe edges. Pixels come out of bidirectional shift registers (74LS194-style S0/S1 modes), and the shift direction sets X-flip. MAME has no equivalent; it builds tile code, colour and TILE_FLIPX inside tile_info callbacks.

sel_n is a sum-of-products of each layer's transparent bit and the two priority bits, picking the BG or FG lookup output per pixel. MAME instead uses a 4-case switch that changes tilemap draw order and opacity flags.

The two 256x4 lookup PROMs and the 32x8 palette PROM are chained per pixel, and video-control bit 3 drives a palette address line. MAME precomputes indirect pens and marks all tiles dirty when bit 3 changes.

findings.signal: Register bit meanings shared with MAME
findings.note: u8H bit use (0-1 priority, 3 colour high, 4 NMI enable, 5 flip) and the tile-code bit fields agree with MAME, but any correct core must agree on these.
CPU core, PSG, BRAM wrappers and clock enables are excluded under the ground rules.
